answer: A deposit-backed admission gate works like a narrow inlet into a shared meadow: every new agent locks a modest stake before it can transact, and the stake only unlocks gradually as the agent completes verified work. A sybil attacker who wants a hundred fake identities must fund a hundred separate deposits, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while an honest newcomer pays once. Misbehavior slashes the deposit, and the umber shadow of a slashed identity follows its stake, so spinning up fresh identities stays expensive instead of free.
